question.problem:
The diagram below shows the function $y=f(x).$ Plot the graph of $y=2f\left(3(x+3)\right)+5.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14215685/assets/b314de8320a82ad5a7bd395da63c6f9bd4348ee2f4fd12c13a090c20fbcdd322.png)
question.worked_solution:
To perform transformations of functions with multiple operations, we must remember the following rule:

1\. First, we perform the transformations *inside* the argument of $f.$ We first carry out horizontal stretches, followed by horizontal translations.

2\. Then, we perform the transformations *outside* the argument of $f.$ We first carry out vertical stretches, followed by vertical translations.

To plot $y=2f\left({3}(x+3)\right)+5,$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=f(x).$

- Stretch it by a scale factor of $\dfrac{1}{3}$ parallel to the $x$-axis to get the graph of $y=f\left({3}x\right).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14215685/assets/92ffae3729220d6eae6cfb96fde2efc93f19b58ad38a5ba36760fb8b38ee8ced.png)

- Then, translate it left by $3$ units to get the graph of $y=f\left({3}(x+3)\right).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14215685/assets/c4fc767f318d276a0178f4ceb2d2550a5141744ca2c3ed8da1f240309d3a1ca0.png)

- Then, stretch it by a scale factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=2f\left(3(x+3)\right).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14215685/assets/143a49c724c30a9e9cf432960fcf7046784a9a881182959875b9805adb0a8c5e.png)

- Finally, translate it up by $5$ units to get the graph of $y=2f\left(3(x+3)\right)+5.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14215685/assets/6d7295138c2821d0d3c479ff9d98e2018bc26493ff09f41fe463cc31cee0907e.png)
